message.content:
**London’s time zones**

| Season | Standard name | Offset from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) |
|--------|-----------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Winter (roughly late October – late March) | **Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)** | UTC ± 0 hours |
| Summer (roughly last Sunday in March – last Sunday in October) | **British Summer Time (BST)** | UTC ± 1 hour |

So:

* In the non‑daylight‑saving period London follows **GMT**, i.e., it is at **UTC+0**.
* During daylight savings London switches one hour ahead to **BST**, i.e., it becomes **UTC+1**.

These rules apply each year unless legislation changes them. If you’re looking up an exact current offset right now, you can check a reliable world clock service or simply add +1 if today falls between the last Sundays of March and October.
